  MINUTES

  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  July 28, 2025

ROLL CALL: At 6:05 p.m., on Monday, July 28, 2025, the Alhambra City Council met in the Council
Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
PRESENT via videoconference:  WANG
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Hembree, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director
of Finance Lieu, Director of Community Development Ho, Director of Public Works and Utilities Ahlen,
Chief of Police Kennedy, Battalion Chief Brown, Director of Library Services LohGuan, Director of
Human Resources Ko, Manager Analyst Alvarez, Code Enforcement Officer Cornejo, Code
Enforcement Supervisor Perez-Garcia, Senior Planner Wu

FLAG SALUTE:  Mayor Lee

LEE: Mayor Lee read the City’s Mission Statement as follows: The City of Alhambra is dedicated to
responsive, creative leadership and quality services, ensuring desirable neighborhoods and a
supportive business environment, while being sensitive to the diversity of our community.

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

COUNCIL BUSINESS

  City Attorney MONTES delivered a staff report. On July 28, 2025, Councilmember WANG
  requested that her Council colleagues vote to allow her participation via video/teleconference
  at the July 28, 2025 City Council meeting due to a physical injury which limited her mobility.
  Under current Government Code section 54953(f), this was allowable action if approved by
  the City Council.

  Ms. WANG confirmed that there were no other adults present in the room with her at her
  location.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved Councilmember Wang’s request by motion and
  voted to allow her to participate and vote remotely via video/teleconference in City Council
  meetings due to an emergency medical reason under Government Code Section 54953(f).

CEREMONIAL

1.  CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE: RICK VERGARA – F2M25-3

  Rick Vergara who recently retired after 27 years of faithful and loyal service to the Public Works
  Department and the City of Alhambra. Mr. VERGARA recounted his many years with the City
  and expressed gratitude to Council and staff. Mayor LEE presented a Certificate of Service
  plaque to Mr. Vergara for his outstanding work for the City.

  Public Comment:  “Dick Yo” spoke regarding the benefits of retirement and the
  responsibility of public works employees as well as the responsibility of citizens. He went on
  to criticize Los Angeles County and Los Angeles City leadership.

PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-AGENDIZED ITEMS (TIME LIMITATIONS: 5 MINUTES PER
SPEAKER, 30 MINUTES TOTAL) – F2M25-4

  1) Freddy BARBARINI, 1727 Lemon St., spoke against the use of illegal fireworks, expressed
  frustration at the escalation of illegal fireworks, and requested action by the City.

  2) Cindy GUTIERREZ, 931 S. Atlantic Blvd, representing the Community Health Alliance,

  5) Miss Amy spoke regarding illegal fireworks, a stolen Alhambra Police cruiser, the Alhambra

PUBLIC HEARING

2.  PUBLIC HEARING RELATING TO THE COLLECTION OF COSTS AND FEES FOLLOWING
  WEED ABATEMENT AT 804 S. SIXTH STREET – F2M25-41, N2M25-95, R2M25-28, M2M25-
  119

  This was the time and place set by Notice No. N2M25-95 for the City Council to hold a public
  hearing relating to the collection of costs and fees following weed abatement at 804 S. Sixth
  Street. Code Enforcement Officer CORNEJO delivered a staff report and presentation, which
  is on file in the City Clerk’s office. On August 22, 2024, the City received a complaint regarding
  overgrown vegetation at 804 S. Sixth Street (the “Property”). Upon inspection it was confirmed
  2
7-28-25
   that the conditions of the property were in violation of Section 6.24.020 of the Alhambra
  Municipal Code (AMC) with overgrown weeds and vegetation. On August 26, 2024, a Notice
  of Violation was issued by mail and posted on the Property. No remedial action was taken.
  Numerous attempts were made by Code Enforcement to remedy the situation with no success.
  Overgrown weeds and vegetation are health and safety hazards. It is a property owner’s duty
  to keep their property free from weeds, which constitute a public nuisance under Section
  6.24.020 of the AMC. Once the City issues a Notice to Abate per Section 6.24.030 of the AMC,
  the City has the authority to abate the nuisance itself to ensure the health and safety of the
  community is maintained per Section 6.24.070. On March 17, 2025, the Code Enforcement
  Division and accompanying City officials served and executed the Inspection and Abatement
  Warrant and conducted an abatement of the overgrown vegetation to rid the Property of health
  and safety violations.

  Section 6.24.100 of the AMC requires that the record of costs be submitted to the City Council
  prior to June 30th of the fiscal year in which the abatement work was performed, which was
  satisfied on June 23, 2025. A hearing on the confirmation of such costs must be held prior to
  July 30th of such year. As of this date, the total cost incurred by the City – including contractor
  services, attorney involvement, and City staff time was $30,660.45. Per Section 6.24.130 of
  the AMC, Council shall hear evidence surrounding the Agency Lien List, together with any
  objections from the property owners liable for the assessment, and may make any revision,
  correction, or modification to the costs owed. AMC Section 6.24.140 states that the total costs
  confirmed by Council shall constitute a special assessment and a lien against the respective
  lot or parcel of land to which it relates. A special assessment is a tax bill levied by the County
  Auditor Controller’s Office, and a nuisance abatement lien constitutes a claim against the
  property which clouds title to the property and must be paid prior to sale of the property. Both
  types of liens can be foreclosed on in the event of non-payment. City staff recommended that
  the City Council approve both a lien and an assessment to ensure cost recovery, as set forth
  in the AMC.

  Opened Public Hearing: Mayor LEE opened the public hearing.

  Public Comment:
  1) Dick, Yo spoke regarding attorney fees, potential mental health issues, potential racial issues,
  criticized weed abatement programs, and spoke in favor of President Trump. He continued to
  speak against homelessness and criticized illegal immigration.

  2) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., spoke regarding the staff report and the photos
  attached. He continued to discuss the case, Code Enforcement procedures, Fire Department
  procedures, and Los Angeles County fire hazard procedures.

  Closed Public Hearing:  After receiving public comment, Mayor LEE closed the public
  hearing.

  Discussion: Vice Mayor MALONEY outlined action taken, supported staff’s procedure and
  commented that cases such as these were rare. Mr. MALONEY motioned to approve staff
  recommendations, which was seconded by Councilmember MAZA. Councilmember WANG
  and Director of Community Development HO discussed interactions with the property owners
  and determined that there were no language or ability barriers. Mr. HO also stated that the
  owner was properly notified and contacted. Ms. WANG supported the motion to approve and
  also requested staff explore options to identify potential hazardous properties and extend
  outreach to aging property owners. Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER also supported the
  effort of staff and stated that she personally witnessed vermin at the property. Councilmember
  MAZA agreed with Ms. Wang’s comments regarding an aging population and spoke regarding
  past collaboration between the Fire Department and Code Enforcement. He also spoke
  regarding community volunteers and stated that help was available to those that need it. Mayor
  3
7-28-25
   LEE and Mr. HO continued to discuss communication with the property owner and his lack of
  response. Ms. LEE and Mr. MONTES continued to discuss the process of placing a tax lien on
  a property and the removal of the lien.

  Action Taken:  City Council:

  1.  Conducted a public hearing to receive public testimony; and,

  2.  Determined the correctness or reasonableness, or both, of the costs incurred
  ($30,660.45) in the City’s abatement of the nuisance conditions on the property located
  at 804 S. Sixth Street (“Property”); and,

  3.  Authorized a nuisance abatement lien and a special assessment against the Property
  in the amount of the City’s abatement costs (M2M25-119); and,

  4.  Adopted Resolution No. R2M25-28 entitled: A Resolution of the City Council of the
  City of Alhambra, California, confirming a report of abatement costs and authorizing a
  nuisance abatement lien and special tax assessment to be recorded on title against
  804 South 6th Street

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  MALONEY, WANG, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

PRESENTATION

3.  CITY OF ALHAMBRA OBJECTIVE DESIGN STANDARDS AND DESIGN GUIDELINES
  PROJECT – F2M24-42

  Senior Planner WU delivered the staff report and Jamie WILLIAMS, from RRM Design Group
  delivered a presentation, which are on file in the City Clerk’s office. As part of the ongoing
  Objective Design Standards and Design Guidelines work effort, the City, in partnership with
  RRM Design Group, completed a series of community outreach and engagement efforts over
  the last several months. The purpose of the outreach and engagement efforts were to inform
  the community about the scope of the project, describe the importance of objective design
  standards and design guidelines, and solicit feedback on design topics to inform future design
  guidelines for specific focus areas, including the East Main Corridor (EMC), Central Business
  District (CBD), West Main Corridor, and Valley Boulevard. Objective Design Standards for
  multi-family residential development would also be created in this work effort, be applied city-
  wide to ensure high quality design standards, and be aligned with State mandated housing
  legislation which requires local jurisdictions to eliminate any subjectivity in the architectural
  review of housing developments. The new multi-family objective design standards for multi-
  family developments will provide additional clarity to architects and designers so that future
  projects will be complimentary to existing neighborhoods. Overall, the community outreach
  series generated valuable feedback that RRM will incorporate as they move forward with
  finalizing the updated Objective Design Standards and finalizing the development of specific
  Design Guidelines for the identified focus areas (Valley Boulevard, West Main/CBD, and
  EMC). Following the presentation, the project team would move forward with preparing focus
  area Design Guidelines and finalizing an update of the existing objective design standards to
  be presented for adoption through the public hearing process.

  Public Comment:

  4
7-28-25
   1) Jennifer NG, S. Cordova St., reported on her recent walks through East Main Corridor with
  neighbors and discussed their observations of the original diverse architectural elements
  present. She urged staff and Council to review the present elements rather than a strict reliance
  on Spanish style. She thanked staff for receiving input from the public.

  2) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., echoed Ms. Ng’s comments regarding their walks
  through the East Main Corridor and also discussed their observations of the original
  architectural elements. He also thanked staff and the consultant for receiving input from the
  public.

  Discussion: Vice Mayor MALONEY and Director of Community Development HO
  discussed the next steps in the process of adopting the Objective Design Standards and
  Design Guidelines and the difference between the two guidelines. Councilmember
  ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. HO discussed the changes to Valley Boulevard and potential
  historic storefronts. Councilmember MAZA and Mr. HO discussed objective design guidelines
  for stand alone commercial properties. Councilmember WANG thanked staff, the consultant,
  and the community for their work and discussed Valley Boulevard design guideline examples
  with Ms. WILLIAMS. Mayor LEE discussed the background of this item, the next steps of the
  process, and the benefits of adopting design standards and guidelines.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed this report.

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 4 – 32)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda, with the exception of Item No. 4, 6. 7, 8, 10, 11, 17, 18, 19,
20, and 22, were considered by the City Council to be routine and were enacted by one motion.

4.  CONSIDERATION OF RESOLUTION DISCUSSING FEDERAL IMMIGRATION
  ENFORCEMENT ACTIVITIES – F2M5-7, R2M25-29

  Following a robust discussion at the July 7, 2025 special meeting of the City Council, it was
  requested staff bring back a resolution that revises the “Community’s Resolution,” which draft
  was based on legal review and ability to implement and included the draft statement
  “Supporting Alhambra’s Immigrant Community”. Changes to the “Community’s Resolution” as
  well as a draft version of Resolution No. R2M25-29 were outlined in the July 28, 2025 staff
  report by the Deputy City Manager.

  Public Comment:

  The following people spoke in favor of the resolution and immigration protections:
  1) Shirley TATSUNO, 1408 S. Fifth St., also spoke regarding the Japanese incarceration during
  WWII and distributed handouts to Council from her recent trip to Manzanar National Historic
  Site.

  2) Lewis MCCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., also spoke regarding the need for immigration
  reform, the need to update citizenship requirements, as well as distributed handouts to Council.

  3) Michael A. JONES, a resident of District 1, representing Working Families Party, also
  expressed that he believed the resolution was more watered down than he hoped with regards
  to local monitoring and documentation.

  The following people spoke against the resolution but supported immigration
  protections:
  1) Miss Amy
  5
7-28-25
   2)  Beverly Murata, 13 Palmetto Dr.
  3)  Pablo Garcia, a resident of Alhambra
  4)  Sean Wakase, 3214 Dorchester Ave, Los Angeles
  5)  Marcos, representing the Peace and Freedom Party of Los Angeles
  6)  Pranit, a resident of Alhambra

  The following people spoke against the resolution and immigration:
  1) Dick

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER discussed the resolution, the City and
  Council’s support for immigrants in Alhambra, and addressed Marcos’s comments. Vice Mayor
  MALONEY and City Attorney MONTES discussed the points regarding warrants and provided
  clarification regarding the legal requirements and process for warrants. Mr. MALONEY, Mr.
  MONTES, and Police Chief KENNEDY also discussed means to address concerns about
  masked and unidentified individuals taking people into supposed custody. Chief KENNEDY
  reiterated that there were zero immigration raids in Alhambra which were reported to the Police
  Department. He also reiterated that officers would respond to 911 calls regarding questionable
  immigration enforcement and that they would verify the identity of the federal agents. Mr.
  MALONEY reiterated that should any residents feel unsafe or that there are any suspicious
  activities, that they call the Police Department. He echoed Ms. Andrade-Stadler’s comments
  regarding Council’s stance on immigration rights. He discussed the limitations of local and
  state governments against federal policies and spoke in support of the Resolution.
  Councilmember MAZA supported Ms. Andrade-Stadler’s comments. He went on to discuss
  the limitations of local government and the changes made to the Resolution. Councilmember
  WANG echoed her colleagues’ comments regarding limitations of local government and
  specifically Ms. Andrade-Stadler’s comments. She spoke in support of the Resolution. Mayor
  LEE supported the Resolution, echoed her colleagues’ comments regarding the limitations of
  local government, and discussed the need for federal immigration polices to be reformed. Ms.
  LEE discussed the title of the resolution and suggested that the word “aggressive” be
  reconsidered. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER, Ms. LEE, and Mr. MALONEY discussed the title.
  Ms. WANG suggested changing it to “unwarranted aggressive and non-transparent tactics.”
  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER motioned to approve the Resolution and Mr. MALONEY seconded
  it.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved Resolution No. R2M25-29 entitled: Alhambra
  condemns aggressive and non-transparent federal immigration enforcement tactics, reaffirms
  commitment to constitutional and community safety principles, and directs proactive local
  response measures

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

5.  AWARD CONTRACT: MOBILE DATA COMPUTERS (MDC) – F2M26-6B, C2M25-31,
M2M25-103

  The Police Department has utilized mobile data computers (MDC) as a vital communication
  tool between dispatchers and officers. The existing MDCs were over five years old and had
  become outdated and obsolete. Getac Technology Corporation submitted a quote of
  $120,744.72 for 23 Getac S510 MDCs (including mounting hardware and installation) under
  the State of California Sourcewell Coorperative Agreement Number 090122-GET. These
  agreements are available to all State of California government agencies. In accordance with
  Alhambra Municipal Code 3.36.080(B)(3), the City Council may approve purchases through or
  6
7-28-25
   in conjunction with another public agency’s purchase of the same supplies or equipment.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to Getac Technology Corporation in an amount not to
  exceed $120,744.72 for the purchase of mobile data computers and related equipment and
  installation; authorized the Chief of Police to execute said agreement; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary finalize Council’s action. (M2M25-103)

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

6.  ACCEPT DONATION: TILE MURAL – F2M25-12, M2M25-104

  The Haas family had an accounting office located at 106 and 108 S. First Street, where they
  conducted business for many years. During that time, they acquired a tile mural from Muralist
  Guillermo Wagner Granizo and displayed it in the office. Mr. Ken Haas would like to donate
  the art piece to the City of Alhambra. The new Community Center might be a suitable
  placement for the tile mural.

  Public Comment:  Shirley TATSUNO, 1408 S. Fifth St., spoke in support of the mural.
  She also discussed Ms. Ng’s public comment during Item No. 3.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted with gratitude a gift of an 8-foot by 5-foot tile
  mural, done by prominent California Tile Muralist Guillermo Wagner Granizo, depicting The
  Alhambra in Granada, Spain from Ms. Tricia Haas and Mr. Ken Haas; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M25-104)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  WANG, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  AUTHORIZE RFP: PROFESSIONAL CONSULTING SERVICES FOR PREPARATION
OF THE CITY’S OFFICIAL REPORTS AND PLANS UNDER THE U.S. DEPARTMENT  OF
HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT (HUD) – F2M25-43, RFP2M25-11

  In accordance with Federal law, the City is required to submit an Annual Action Plan and
  Consolidated Annual Performance Evaluation Report (CAPER), outlining the City's
  Community Development Block Grant and HOME funded activities. Staff requested the City
  Council authorize staff to solicit proposals for professional services to assist staff in preparing
  the City of Alhambra’s Annual Action Plan and Consolidated Annual Performance Evaluation
  Report (CAPER) for the following program years: 2025-2026 CAPER; 2026-2027 Annual
  Action Plan; 2026-2027 CAPER; 2027-2028 Annual Action Plan; 2027-2028 CAPER; 2028-
  2029 Annual Action Plan; and, assist City with interface and record keeping with IDIS System
  and HEROS.

  Public Comment:

7-28-25

8.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: CONSTRUCTION OF THE POPPY PARK PROJECT –
  F2M24-57, N2M25-98

  On December 9, 2024, the City Council approved a contract with Hirsch & Associates, Inc. for
  professional engineering and design services to provide plans, specifications, and bid
  documentation for the Poppy Park Project. On June 25, 2025, staff and representatives from
  Hirsch & Associates, held a community meeting with renderings and design layouts for the
  Poppy Park Project and received feedback that has been incorporated into the plans. The
  specifications and bid documentation for the Poppy Park Project were completed. Bids would
  be due no later than 10:30 a.m. on September 11, 2025 in the office of the City Clerk, and
  would be opened at 11:00 a.m. that same day.

  Public Comment:  Dick spoke against the item and supported use of funds for homeless
  support services.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids to
  prospective contractors for the construction of the Poppy Park Project; and, directed staff to

  Noes:  NONE

  REPLACEMENT IMPROVEMENT PROJECT – F2M25-34, N2M25-53, C2M25-32,
M2M25-105

  On May 12, 2025, the City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids for the

10.  CONTRACT EXTENSION FOR PROFESSIONAL AUDIT SERVICES – F2M22-21,
  C2M22-13, M2M25-106

11.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION: ALHAMBRA PARK POOL IMPROVEMENT PROJECT –
F2M22-37, C2M24-3, M2M25-107

  On January 8, 2024, the City Council awarded a contract to Tom’s Construction in the amount
  of $712,00.00 for the Alhambra Park Pool Improvement Project. The project was funded by
  the Los Angeles County Regional Park and Open Space District in the amount of $963,000.00.
  There were three change orders to the project. The change orders included: Change Order
  No. 1: Handrails to match ramp railing; Change Order No. 2: Upper pool ramp, front entrance
  tile, and front sliding gate; and, Change Order No. 3: automatic doors, handrail extension,
  paint, and countertops. The change orders totaled $122,150.00, which brought the contract
  costs to $834,150.00. Staff inspected this project, and all work was completed in accordance
  with the City’s requirements and specifications. As such, it would be appropriate for the City
  Council to accept this project as complete.

  Public Comment:  Dick spoke against the item and discussed drought in California.
  Discussion:  None.
  9
7-28-25
   Action Taken:  City Council accepted the work of Tom’s Construction for the Alhambra
  Park Pool Improvement Project as complete in the amount of $834,150.00; directed the City
  Clerk to file a Notice of Completion with the County of Los Angeles for recordation; instructed
  the Finance Director to release the 5 percent retention 35 days from the date of recordation, if
  no liens are filed; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s
  action. (M2M25-107)

  Ayes:  WANG, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE

12.  RESOLUTION APPROVING THE APPLICATION OF GRANT FUNDS UNDER THE
  LAND AND WATER CONSERVATION FUND FOR THE STORY PARK ALL-
  INCLUSIVE PLAYGROUND – F2M25-18, R2M25-27, M2M25-108

  Staff was in the process of preparing a grant application to the Land and Water Conservation
  Fund for the purchase of an all-inclusive playground at Story Park. The funding request of
  $1,058,937 was based on preliminary estimates for the equipment. The project would replace
  the current play structure which has been in place for over twenty years. The new playground
  would complement the Story Park renovations (Serenity Circle) that were scheduled to be
  completed in 2026. The playground equipment, when installed, would enhance the park
  experience for children of all ages and abilities.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M25-27 entitled: A Resolution
  of the City of Alhambra approving the application for the Land and Water Conservation Fund
  Story Park All Inclusive Playground Equipment Project as required by the Land and Water
  Conservation Fund authorizing a grant request for the replacement of the large playground at
  Story Park; authorized the City Manager, or designee, to execute all grant documents; and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M25-108)

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE

22.  2025 UPDATE TO THE SEWER SYSTEM MANAGEMENT PLAN – F2M7-92, M2M25-115

  In December 2022, the State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB) adopted the
  Statewide General Waste Discharge requirements for Sanitary Sewer Systems under Order
  No. 2022-0103-DWQ. This Order became effective on June 5, 2023. All federal and state
  agencies, municipalities, counties, districts, and other public entities that own or operate
  sanitary sewer systems greater than one mile in length that collect and/or convey untreated or
  partially treated wastewater to a publicly owned treatment facility in the State of California were
  required to comply with the terms of this order. The goal of the order was to facilitate proper
  management of all sanitary sewer systems and prevent sewage spills through the
  development of a Sewer System Management Plan (SSMP). The order also required that the
  SSMP be updated every five years and adopted at a public meeting held by the governing
  body. The last update of the City’s SSMP was approved by City Council in April of 2019.
